name: Does the HSNS predict behaviour beyond group membership?
description:
A preliminary memo reports that the Hypersensitive Narcissism Scale predicts an independently measured behavioural outcome in a labelled training sample. A held-out sample has the same questionnaire, group variable and outcome. In both, responses and outcomes are matched by `participant_id`.

Answer three questions by these rules, where the latent coefficient is the trait's coefficient on the outcome:

  group_adjusted    `supported` if the latent coefficient, adjusted for group, is at least 0.10 in absolute value in both samples.
  within_group      `replicates` if, in the training sample, the latent coefficient is at least 0.10 in absolute value in each group and the two estimates differ by no more than 0.06.
  holdout           `generalizes` if the group-adjusted latent coefficient changes by no more than 0.06 between training and holdout.

Also list every item whose direct association with the outcome, after accounting for the trait and group, is at least 0.10 in training but no more than 0.05 in the holdout.
submission_format:
A single JSON object:

{
  "model_syntax": "F =~ HSNS1+...+HSNS10\nbehavior ~ F + gender",
  "association": {
    "group_adjusted": "supported|not_supported",
    "within_group": "replicates|does_not_replicate",
    "holdout": "generalizes|does_not_generalize"
  },
  "unstable_items": ["<item identified from the evidence>"]
}

The model must cover every HSNS item, include `behavior`, and include both the
latent factor and `gender` in the behavioural regression. The scorer refits the
submitted measurement model in the training and holdout samples and performs
the within-group and item checks from that model.
